section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1979
title: 6 ## Causes of Accidental Deaths The total accidental deaths recorded during 1979 have been classified under two broad categories: (A) accidental deaths due to natural causes like lightning, heat stroke, floods, land slides, cold and exposure and cyclone, and (B) accidental deaths due to other causes like mishaps in factories, road accidents, railway accidents, air crashes, house collapse and boats capsizing. Category (A) accounted for 3·6 percent of total accidental deaths recorded in 1979 in comparison to 4·5 percent in 1978. Under this category, the maximum number of deaths in 1979 were due to ‘Lightning’ (1496) followed by ‘Land slides’ (753), ‘Heat Stroke’ (594), ‘Floods’ (567), ‘Cold & Exposure’ (318) and ‘Cyclone’ (248). Category (B) claimed 96·4 percent of the total accidental deaths registered during 1979 as against 95·5 percent registered during 1978. Under this category the maximum number of accidental deaths in 1979 were under the head ‘Drowning’ (22879) followed by ‘Accidental Deaths on Roads’ (18273), ‘In Railways’ (11126), ‘By Fire’ (10282), ‘By Poisoning’ (5845), ‘Killed or bitten by Animals’ (2810), ‘By Fire Arms’ (1332), ‘By House Collapse’ (991), ‘In Mines and Quarry Disasters’ (628), ‘In Factories’ (502), ‘By Explosion’ (308), ‘By Boats Capsizing’ (306), and in ‘Air crashes’ (70). ‘Miscellaneous’ causes recorded a total number of 29659 cases during 1979 as against 32064 cases in 1978. During 1979; Drowning accounted for 21·0 percent of the total accidental deaths in India, followed by accidents on roads due to motor vehicles (14·1%), ‘On Railways’
